scope_note: VENUE-ONLY BY DESIGN. This payload deliberately carries no depth, crossing, redemption path or rating; those belong to PegTracker's ladder. Absence of `depth` here is a declaration, not a failed write -- a consumer should keep the ladder from its other source. Primary redemption (the Fraxtal route) is NOT published here; its owner is not yet assigned. Pool ownership is in `lp_ownership`.

finding_meanings.venues_found: Pools at or above the $1,000 TVL floor were found.
finding_meanings.none_found: Searched, and nothing at or above the floor was found: a market fact as far as the indexer reaches.

enumeration.chain_count_note: FLOOR, not a census: chains are the asset's CoinGecko platforms. A deployment CoinGecko does not list is not queried here.
enumeration.live_venue_count_basis: Derived from venues[].is_live. The per-venue field is the single source; this integer is a convenience and cannot disagree with it. ⚠️ 9 venue(s) carry no established verdict, so this is a FLOOR of confirmed-live venues, not a total. An unestablished venue is UNKNOWN, not dead.
enumeration.dashboard_scope_basis: The first liquidity headline is Ethereum only. Other deployments are searched and labelled outside_scope: an Ethereum enumeration says nothing about exits there, and a pool there is no exit for an Ethereum holder.

reason_meanings.below_tvl_floor: Reported TVL under $1,000: dust. Left out of `venues` and every total.
reason_meanings.duplicate_listing: The same pool address returned twice by the indexer; kept once in `venues`.
reason_meanings.tvl_exceeds_supply: Kept in `venues`, but its TVL is out of every total: it exceeds the token's whole value on the chain.
reason_meanings.tvl_exceeds_onchain_custody: Kept in `venues`, but its TVL is out of every total: it is far above what the pool holds on-chain.
reason_meanings.counter_token_value_implausible: Kept in `venues`, but its TVL is out of every total: it rests on a price for a token with no real market value.

venue_diagnostics.volume_policy: 24h volume is published as context and is never a reason to reject a pool: a quiet day is not a dead pool (backing-monitor's fleet venue rule 5).
venue_diagnostics.dedup_basis: One source (GeckoTerminal) keyed by pool address, so the same pool cannot enter twice. Liquidity wrappers that re-list a pool (Convex, Yearn, StakeDAO, Beefy, Aura) are kept out of `venues` and marked `lp_wrapper` in `non_swap_listings`.

not_read.semantics: Whole-pool indexer TVL of pools whose balances could not be read: NOT counter-side.

absorbing_side.semantics: Counter-asset units held by the pools, by what they are. Do NOT add circular_counter to independent_exit: a counter backed by this asset fails with it. None of this is depth.

lp_ownership.source: eth_call totalSupply/balanceOf on each LP token and on its Convex reward contract, at one block; Convex pools from the Booster's poolInfo for every pid at the same block.

holders_read.0x4b45d73b83686e69d08e61105fdb7f7b51f41b: Frax sfrxUSD controller (3-of-6 Safe, no delay)

lp_ownership.semantics: Who owns the LP shares of each pool, read at one block. A pool whose LP is almost all one operator's is depth that operator can withdraw in one transaction: it is real at the block and not durable. Ownership is not depth, and owned inventory is never added to treasury cash, redemption inventory or strategy withdrawal limits: the same frxUSD would be counted twice.
limitations: Only the named holder is read. The rest of each pool's LP is 'other holders', not broken down.
Convex is the only staking wrapper read; LP staked in a Curve gauge directly, StakeDAO, Yearn or elsewhere counts as other holders.
Ownership can change in any later block. A withdrawal needs one controller Safe transaction; no delay was established.
Coin units are the pool's balances(i); attributable units are a pro-rata claim, not what a withdrawal would return after fees.
